method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file again: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (10 lines, gist item), the three inputs (3 × 10 lines) and the LS3 form, the six H1 texts, the strategy card, the 8 redemittel, the Sp1 task (instructions, situation, 5 cards, aiRole.personaDe, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 9 modelTurns), the S1 task (situation, taskDe, 5 labels, 4 checklist lines, model), the 3 check lines, story, fact f01, every endLine, modelSentence, aussprache line, promptDe, option and explanation.de, the 36 u02 cards of a1.1/lexicon.json and the three rule cards the unit shows (rc.negation-nicht, rc.ja-nein-frage, rc.praesens-2). We solved all 94 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line (start gist 1; LS1 and LS2 each 5 input + 4 structured + 11 pool + 5 reserve; LS3 5 + 4 + 11 + 6 reserve, the new ls3-r06 included; 6 H1; 8 Check; 3 proof) and the 5 S1 fields; every key is right. We graded 90 candidate answers with the real grader (src/components/course-v2/grade.js gradeAnswer → src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js), the S1 fields exactly as WritingTaskView.jsx FormTask builds them (type form_fill), and the same FormTask grading on the S1 forms of u01, u05 and u09 (F01). We simulated every proposed accepted-list change with the same grader before recommending it (F01, F02). We measured unknown words with the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms + unknownOnSurface at a1.1-u02 on every read surface (walked and unwalked), on the three rule cards and on the 36 word cards, and ran every placed GRM-04 detector over the surfaces GRM-04 does not read (promptDe, options, explanation.de, endLines, micro-output prompts, story, openingLine, hintWords, modelTurns). Every German line proposed below was checked the same way and against TXT-04's 90 characters. We read the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1, sp1, s1) and the rubrics sd1-sp1 and sd1-s1; every task is original in the SD1 format. We read the can-dos (registries/cando/a1.json), the cast and voices (casts/series.json, casts/a1.json), the story against u01 (cliffhanger, beat), u03 (Folge), u05 (address, Arjun's number), u08 and u12 (Priya's number), the level profile (level-profiles.json a1.1), the grammar spine and the partner prompt the speaking engine builds (netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs buildCoursePartnerPrompt, monologue ABLAUF). We checked the modification times of every owner file r2 routed work to (lexicon.json, rule-cards.json, names.json, casts, grammar-spine.json, rules/, lib-validate/, checkItem.js): none changed after r2; u12 changed shortly before r2 was written. We also ran the level validator on a1.1. Exemplar: u04 and its trail r1–r5 and the u01 trail r1–r3; every class is checked in notes. No 360 px walkthrough was run; that is the walkthrough reviewer's remit. No MCP tool and no git command was used.

findings.problem: The unit side of r2-F02 landed: every entry r2 quoted now passes. The checker rule r2 asked for was not written, so the class is still open, and the next obvious variants fail. A learner who combines two accepted entries („Online-Kurs, nicht in Leipzig“), who copies the situation's own phrase („Izmir in der Türkei“), or who writes a slash gets 0 for a field that a Goethe S1 marker scores 1: the information is right. On top of that, f1 carries exact: 'name', which makes every letter slip WRONG. That contradicts the lane rubric sd1-s1, where spelling costs the point only if meaning suffers. It also contradicts the unit's own f2, where the same missing umlaut („Turkei“) is a TYPO and counts. So one form marks one slip in two ways. §9.4: a defensible second answer not accepted is MAJOR. The class is the method, and it is not u02's alone. The same FormTask grading loses correct entries in the S1 forms of u01, u05 and u09. Four A1.1 units without a rule meets the §9.4 stop-the-line threshold. Every new hand variant only moves the failure to the next variant.
findings.fix: Unit, now: remove exact: 'name' from f1. Wohnort is copied from the text, not spelled; ITM-07 does not require it, and the checker's typo rule then scores „Ismir“ and „Izmir, Turkei“ as TYPO, which FormTask counts. Add no further hand variants. Checker owner, which is what closes the MAJOR: write the form_fill content rule below with its test. findings.proposedRule: form_fill grading in checkItem (type 'form_fill'; test over all registered courses). Fold case, hyphens and the separators „, / ( ) –“. An answer is correct when all of the following hold. (a) It contains an accepted form as a word or as a compound part („Online|kurs“). (b) Every other token is a negation of an alternative that labelDe offers („nicht in Leipzig“), or a word of the situation text that names the same fact („Türkei“, „in der Türkei“, „am Abend“, „mit Priya“, „Leipzig“ after a street). (c) It contains no un-negated alternative from labelDe. Spelling follows the Teil rubric's `spelling` field: under sd1-s1, one letter slip per word is a TYPO and counts. `exact: 'number'` stays digit-exact. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u02 f5 „Online-Kurs, nicht in Leipzig“; f1 „Izmir in der Türkei“ and „Izmir, Turkei“; a1.1-u01 f3 „Izmir, Türkei“; a1.1-u05 f4 „Berliner Str. 21, Leipzig“ and f2 „verheiratet mit Priya“; a1.1-u09 f3 „Freitag, am Abend“. A learner who takes it down letter by letter („B-E-R-I-S-H-A“ or „B E R I S H A“) has every letter right, and the grader marks the answer WRONG, tagged Wortschatz. The course checker already treats „HALLO“, „H A L L O“ and „H-A-L-L-O“ as the same answer (CLAUDE.md; check.js normalizeSpelling). But check.js switches that fold on only when one accepted form is itself spelled (spellingApplies). q01 accepts only „Berisha“, so the fold never runs. §9.4: a defensible second answer not accepted is MAJOR, and here it sits on the proof item. Neither r1 nor r2 tried this input. We scanned every v2 unit: no other typed item has an audio line that spells its key, so this is one instance.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 0 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 6 MINOR. The unit author did everything r2 asked of the unit. All r2 unit edits landed: the ls1-r04 order, the eleven look-ahead strings, the seven phrasing points, the ls3-s01 rewrite and its twin, the Sp1 speed promise, Herr Schaefer's voice and castIn. u12 now agrees on Priya's number. Every one of the 94 keys and 5 form fields is right, H1, Sp1 and S1 are exact to sd1.json, every German-only item surface is now free of welch-, man, ihn and the other r2 look-aheads, and the validator exits 0. No owner or rail acted since r2. The lexicon, rule cards, names registry, cast bible, spine, checker and every validator rule are unchanged. That is why the two MAJORs are both correct answers that the real grader rejects. (1) F01: the S1 form still loses correct entries („Online-Kurs, nicht in Leipzig“, „Izmir in der Türkei“, „Izmir, Turkei“). The same hand-list method also loses correct entries in the S1 forms of u01, u05 and u09, and f1's exact: 'name' contradicts the sd1-s1 spelling rule. This is a stop-the-line class that only the checker owner's form_fill rule can close. (2) F02, new: the Check proof of cd.a1.buchstabieren marks a correct letter-by-letter transcription („B-E-R-I-S-H-A“) wrong, which one accepted form fixes. The six minors are two unit residues and four owner-held items. The unit residues: the new ls3-r06 twin contradicts the story (F03), and ls2-mo exceeds the profile's micro-output band, with three accusative pronouns that no detector sees (F04). The owner-held items: the proof evidence and one persona line (F05), the lexicon and names registry (F06), the rule cards, now with two model-sentence look-aheads (F07), and the rails and detectors (F08). Unit edits needed: drop one exact flag (F01), add one accepted form (F02), change one item (F03), make three to five string edits (F04), and change one persona line (F05). With those edits and the form_fill rule, A returns to 4 and u02 carries 4 owner-held minors (F05, F06, F07, F08), which is within the exit limit.
